1.q: A student notices puddles on the school track dry faster on sunny days than on cloudy days. What is the best next step in the scientific method?
choices: Change several variables at once to save time
Announce that sunlight dries puddles faster, since everyone can see it happen
Write a testable hypothesis about sunlight and drying time
Repeat the observation on cloudy days only, so the results all match

1.q: Two groups test the same hypothesis and get very different results. What should a scientist do first?
choices: Pick the result that agrees with the hypothesis, since it is probably the right one
Average the two results and call it final
Check whether both groups used the same procedure and repeat the test
Throw out the hypothesis right away

1.q: Why is plate tectonics called a theory and not a law?
choices: It explains why things happen and has lots of evidence
It only describes what happens, using an equation
It is a guess that has not been tested enough to become a fact or a law
It is just a guess scientists like

1.q: In an experiment on how slope affects how fast sand slides, which is the independent variable?
choices: The person timing the trials
The kind of sand used in every trial
How fast the sand slides
The angle of the slope

1.q: A scientist builds a model of a volcano. What is the biggest limit of the model?
choices: It is simpler than the real thing, so it can't show every detail
It can never be used to make predictions
It has to be exactly the same size as the real volcano to be useful at all
It is always more accurate than the real volcano

1.q: Why do Earth scientists measure in metric units instead of inches and miles?
choices: Metric units go by tens and scientists everywhere use the same system
Inches can't measure rocks
Metric units are always larger, so big things like mountains are easier to measure
Metric units never need tools

1.q: A hiker says, "The river always floods in spring, so it will flood this year." What kind of reasoning is this?
choices: A conclusion from a controlled experiment
A prediction based on a pattern of past observations
A scientific law, because it describes something that always happens without fail
A scientific law that can't be wrong

1.q: During a lab, a classmate wants to smell a chemical by putting their nose over the beaker. What is the safe advice?
choices: Smell it only if the teacher is out of the room
Waft the air toward your nose with your hand
Sniff it directly so you can tell what it is
Taste a tiny drop instead

1.q: Which question could an oceanographer and a meteorologist both work on?
choices: What a mineral's crystal shape is
How old a mountain range is and how fast it wears down
How far away a galaxy is from our solar system
Warm water feeding hurricanes

1.q: Why do scientists repeat an experiment many times?
choices: To make sure the result is reliable and not a fluke
Because one trial is never allowed
To make the experiment take longer
To change the result until it matches the hypothesis

2.q: Boise is about 43° N, 116° W. Which direction would you travel from Boise to reach the equator?
choices: North
East
West
South

2.q: When it is noon in Idaho (Mountain Time), what time is it one time zone to the east (Central Time)?
choices: Noon

2.q: Why do time zones come out about 15° wide?

Lines of latitude are drawn 15° apart, and each one marks a zone

choices: The east side is flat
The east side is steep

9 km
20 km

A mountain peak, since the circles get smaller toward the top
A straight river

Mapmakers still don't agree on Earth's real shape, so every map guesses
You can't flatten a curved surface without stretching or tearing it
Maps are always drawn too small

2.q: A farmer wants to compare soil type, water rights, and crop yields on the same map layers. Which tool fits best?
choices: GIS
A paper road map
A globe
A compass

2.q: Your phone's GPS finds your location by doing what?
choices: Using one cell tower's name
Measuring the angle of the Sun above the horizon
Timing signals from several satellites
Reading the nearest cell tower's location

3.q: Salt (NaCl) is made of sodium and chlorine bonded together. What is salt?
choices: A single atom
An element
A state of matter
A compound

3.q: Rain falls on a hillside, runs into a stream, and carries sand downhill. Which spheres are interacting?
choices: Atmosphere and biosphere only

Biosphere and geosphere only

3.q: Which element would you find most of if you could sort every atom in Earth's crust?
choices: Iron
Carbon
Gold
Oxygen

A change from an element to a compound
A nuclear change

Fossil fuels and batteries
The Sun and Earth's inner heat

Hydrosphere and geosphere
Atmosphere and biosphere

Only the atmosphere, because the gas and ash go up
None, eruptions stay in one sphere

choices: Yes, because it scratches glass

It is black, and minerals must have a light color

Color
Streak
Hardness

4.q: A mineral breaks into perfect flat sheets that peel apart. What property is that?

Cleavage
Fracture
Luster

Silicates form only in space

Man-made in a lab

A cleavage plane

Marble
Basalt

Clastic
